segments.text: Reserve the suit, the suit, the suit.
Why did they shoot when your hands were clean?
Best man suited for a love they'd never seen.
Kneeling for her, not the life that came between.
He saw angel in that forbidden light.
Forbidden light.
Left the steel and the grime for the wedding night.
Trade the iron for the gold, trade the war for the soul.
Told the council he was whole, took the war for the soul.
Told the council he was whole, took the peaceful road.
Not a threat, not a fight, just a choice in the day.
Left the weapons on the shelf, turned the other way.
He called my phone, voice was shaking with pride.
Said, "Keep the best man suit, I've got nothing to hide.
I'm waiting in the hall." I'm still waiting outside.
Why did they shoot when your hands were clean?
Best man suited for a love they'd never seen.
Kneeling for her, not the life that came between.
Not the life that came between.
Walked to the square where the districts meet.
Unarmed, a ring in his hand on the public street.
One knee down for a vow of forever and grace.
Then the cowards struck from the shadows of the place.
He died on one knee, clean hands in the air.
A man of honor in a world that didn't care.
Cowards, you couldn't face a heart that was whole.
So you traded his life just to keep your control.
Cowards.
Cowards.
You're cowards.
He was a man.
You're nothing.
You're nothing.
Screaming.
Why did they shoot when your hands were clean?
Best man suited for a love they'd never seen.
Kneeling for her, not the life that came between.
Not the life that came between.
Rings replace the weapons.
That's the promise.
Rest now.
